typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style EMObservation.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style EMObservation.

recognitionRules: Use a simple Arial evidence map with clear requirement and proof fields.
Keep forwarding scope visible above the record.
Separate direct experience from transferable experience and unknowns.
Use concise source pointers rather than unexplained ratings.

principles: Name the work and the contribution before describing personal qualities.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Match the requirement to a record someone can inspect.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid unsupported expertise labels and turning prototypes into shipped outcomes.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: I made this part; the team decided what happened next.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE RELEVANT RECORD in Arial with a small monospaced evidence ID. No target or ranking badge.
invariants: Use a simple Arial evidence map with clear requirement and proof fields.
Keep forwarding scope visible above the record.
Separate direct experience from transferable experience and unknowns.
adaptations: A role-specific version changes the requirement column while preserving source facts.
A forwarded version retains scope and contact context.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
